question: Is the North American transformer shortage real and durable through 2030?
answer:
Real, and now visibly split by segment.
• Substation and power units are still scarce: municipal records show a ~130-week median quoted lead time, and WoodMac's 2026 deficits are 15% for power and 8% for substation units.
• Single-phase distribution is loosening: stock quotes run 6-13 weeks and rebuilt units 4-12 weeks.
• New 3-phase pad-mounts were still at 40-50 weeks in early 2026 (W).

Whether it lasts to 2030 depends on the 2027-29 wave. That wave is later in mid-power and earlier in pad-mount than the headlines suggest.

question: Are transformer prices still rising?
answer: Yes. Index levels are confirmed at records: WPU117409 was 381.783 in July, up 4.6% in one month, and PCU335311 was flat in August at 475.065. Round 1's YoY rates of +7.6-8.7% were not re-checked. Buyers are paying PPI escalators and premiums for speed. Base case: mid-single-digit nominal growth, arriving in steps and mostly passing through costs.

question: Are maker margins expanding?
answer:
Yes at the EBITDA level through Q2 2026, mainly from operating leverage and, in power transformers, from price and mix:
• Forgent: 24.4%.
• HD Hyundai: 25.1%.
• Hyosung: 15.7%, +490 bp.
• GE Vernova Electrification: 18.4%, +700 bp organic.
• Hammond: 16.4%.

Gross margins at distribution makers are flat to down; Forgent fell from ~36.9% to ~35.1%. Hubbell Utility was flat as inflation and tariffs offset price. Q3 is the first quarter with the full copper and oil step.

question: Will EO 14421 hand domestic builders a large new market?
answer:
Not in distribution. EO 14421 covers bulk-power equipment at ≥69 kV, excludes local distribution, and bans nothing until DOE finds undue risk in a specific transaction.

Where it does reach:
• 69-138 kV substation units, with no MVA floor.
• Chinese-owned firms anywhere, through an ownership test.
• Installed equipment, which DOE may order removed.

Most of the substitution goes to Korea, Mexico, Brazil and India, none of which is covered.

question: Does trade policy protect a new US plant?
answer:
Distribution: Section 232 charges 25% from all origins (round 1; not re-verified). But Chinese-owned firms are localizing (JST, Eaglerise) and pay nothing on units built in the US.

Power: 15% through 2027 (Annex III listing confirmed, rate secondary-sourced), plus 0-4.32% Korean antidumping on units of 60 MVA and up.

Cores: imported cores may pay 25% or 50% (unresolved). That would cost a US large-unit builder that imports cores 5-10 of its 15 points of shelter (computed).

question: Who would a US plant displace?
answer:
Mostly allies, near-shore suppliers and foreign-owned US plants:
• Power: Mexico, Brazil and Korea supplied 57% of >100 MVA import units in 2025 (unverified series).
• Distribution: Eaglerise underbid US distributors by 18-23% at Lafayette, Korean makers hold places on Austin Energy's $200M supply contracts, and Jinpan's JST sells ~$360M a year (annualized) through its US entity.

question: Will the incumbents' 2027-29 capacity wave close the gap?
answer:
It depends on the segment:
• 3-phase pad-mount: largely closed by 2027-28. PTT's new pad-mount plant, JST, Giga, Eaton, ERMCO and Eaglerise all add capacity, and Forgent says it can support ~2x its FY27 revenue guide.
• 10-160 MVA: later and smaller than announced. Gallman nets ≈1x Crystal Springs in 2029, Rincon is +50% by March 2027, Muscle Shoals is unverified and Niagara is pre-construction. Howard and Prolec are on schedule, though.
• LPT: slipping. Siemens moved to 2027, and South Boston possibly to 2029.

question: Can a new builder secure core steel?
answer:
Core steel is still the hardest input to secure:
• Butler's +25% GOES output is now a $170M project due in 2028, per the CEO.
• Cliffs disclosed no GOES price or tonnage, and Weirton is cancelled.
• Imported cores pay 25% or 50% (unresolved).

Plan on two North American core suppliers and an amorphous option.

question: Is labor a binding constraint?
answer:
Yes for 2027-28:
• Seven plants hiring in that window announce 4,388 jobs, 1.2x the 3,600 coil winders in all of NAICS 3353 (2023).
• Contracted average wages are $65-72k, 52-56% above county averages.
• Hitachi is building worker housing, and Eaton relies on state pre-hire training.

QCEW headcount is still missing.

question: Is distribution softening while large power stays scarce?
answer: Partly established. Buyer data supports loosening in single-phase and stock units, but not in new 3-phase pad-mounts. It also confirms substation and large units are still scarce. The round-1 trigger of 3-phase bids under 20 weeks has not tripped.

question: Buy or build?
answer:
Buy, convert or expand. Use greenfield only for distribution, and only in an existing building. Benchmarks:
• ERMCO bought a finished 566k sq ft shell for $91M (~$161/sq ft).
• Central Moloney leased 140k sq ft and spent ~$25M.
• Eaton is converting a distribution center with a $10M state grant.

Scale assets clear at 12.9-14.1x EBITDA (Prolec), against 5.9-8.8x for lower-middle-market manufacturing. But qualified medium-power targets are scarce.

question: Is demand durable through 2030?
answer:
Yes, and it is now partly countable in units:
• ~27 ERCOT 765/345 kV banks (2030-32 and later).
• ~50-160 US GSUs a year.
• 460-890 MV/LV units and 9-22 HV/MV units per GW of data-center load; ERCOT has 9.5 GW approved, and PJM expects +65.7 GW by 2036.
• NREL projects +160-260% distribution capacity by 2050.

Utility distribution-substation counts are still missing.

question: Will federal money or federal purchasing help a new builder?
answer:
Not in the base case:
• DPA PD 2026-10 names transformers and core steel, but no solicitation or award was found, and Title III may have sunset on Sep 30, 2026 (W).
• 48C is fully allocated.
• EDF has not lent to a grid-equipment maker.
• There is no strategic reserve.

Federal buying (WAPA, USACE) is for custom GSU and LPT units, often through installing integrators.

question: Do incentives change the siting decision?
answer: No. Disclosed state and local awards are 0.8-6.4% of capex, or 9.4% at Niagara if NYPA's award is counted. Only 48C lifted one project (Siemens) to ~17%, and 48C is gone. Labor and existing buildings decide where plants go.
